acceptance.browser_process_crash: PASS - Chromium's CDP Browser.crash command terminated the owned browser process; Playwright observed browser disconnection.
acceptance.pending_operation_recovery: PASS - the user-reported application stage and append-only history were committed before the browser crash while the HTTP response was intentionally held.
acceptance.fresh_browser_readback: PASS - a replacement Chromium process and fresh context recovered the same manual stage/history from the unchanged durable store.
acceptance.no_false_submission: PASS - application submission state and confirmation remained unchanged/absent; the stage is explicitly a user report.
acceptance.external_activity: PASS - the browser was restricted to the synthetic local API; no employer request or submission occurred.
acceptance.full_requirement: PARTIAL - product-worker, Chromium renderer and whole Chromium browser-process crash cases are evidenced; physical host restart remains NOT_RUN.

validation.local_protocol_probe: PASS - Browser.crash disconnected the owned browser, and a replacement Chromium process launched successfully.
validation.frontend_dependency_result: PASS - lockfile dependencies installed; zero vulnerabilities. Vitest warned that Node 25.9.0 is outside its declared engine range.
validation.full_python_suite: NOT_RUN - test/evidence-only browser-crash slice; the complete affected browser and API integration modules were run.

environment.database: Temporary synthetic SQLite database; API process remained running across actual Chromium browser-process termination and replacement.
environment.docker_postgresql: NOT_RUN - no database code or migration changed.

limitations: CDP Browser.crash terminated the isolated Chromium process; this did not restart Windows or validate survival of a host restart.
No production source changed because the existing durable application tracking path recovered correctly after a real browser-process crash.
Issue #9 / MJ-REQ-008 remains OPEN/PARTIAL until physical host restart and any remaining acceptance cases are independently evidenced.
